newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends stable amid foreign fund influx.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends stable amid foreign fund influx.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar closed little changed against its U.S. counterpart on Thursday, as foreign fund inflows almost balanced importers' U.S. dollar demand, dealers said.
The local unit ended at T$27.522 against Wednesday's T$27.520 close.
Turnover through dealers was an active US$263.5 million.
Dealers said Thursday's U.S. dollar buying was partly reflecting the strength of the greenback overseas.
"Because of recent stock market rallies, foreign funds have persistently entered," said one dealer.
The Taiwan stock index, which has surged nearly 1,150 points or 16.6 percent in 1997 alone, gained 0.77 percent on Thursday on frenzied turnover of T$174 billion to close at 8,081.00.

Dealers said even domestic investors had been contributing to the Taiwan dollar's strength -- selling their local U.S. dollar holdings to raise more Taiwan dollar cash to pour into the sizzling stock market.
With local stock market factors offsetting the U.S. dollar's strength overseas, dealers said they expected a stable trading range of T$27.51-27.54 for Friday.
